summary: Mount Ireland: 1916 cabin on Bald Mountain, renamed 1917; blasted off in 1957 for a CL-100 cab; staffed each summer and reached by a 3.5-mile hike.

facts.design: CL-100 13x13 all-steel ground cab (built 1957) on the summit; replaced a 1916 cabin with a rooftop fire-finder and a later cupola
facts.agency: US Forest Service, Wallowa-Whitman National Forest (Whitman District)

access.note: Staffed in summer. The public trail reaches it on foot from a Road 100 trailhead. The sources read do not say whether the cab is open to visitors.

visit.trail_note: From Sumpter, follow the Elkhorn Scenic Byway west 11.7 miles, turn right onto gravel Road 7370, then turn right on Road 100 for 0.2 miles to the trailhead on the left, where a berm blocks an old road. Hike of 3.5 miles with about 2,300 ft of elevation gain (2023 visit page).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 8,197 ft (2,498 m); firelookout.com, the 2023 visit page and the 2021 news report give 8,346 ft. The record keeps the NHLR figure (2498.4 m), as the brief did.
NHLR calls the 1957 cab a ground cab, the record's kind; the 2023 visit page is labelled a steel tower. Both are shown in the story.
Forest Lookouts dates the cupola to 1928 (roof raised); firelookout.com says a cupola was added 'later'. The record uses 1928 from the Forest Lookouts page, which does not cite a source for it.

notes_for_editor: Brief's record checks: registration July 5, 2022 and US 1338 / OR 153 are confirmed on the NHLR page; the 1916 build date is confirmed. The brief's 'ground' kind matches NHLR, but a 2023 visit page calls it a steel tower. No access level is firmly established: the sources say the lookout is staffed and reachable on a 3.5-mile trail, but not whether the cab is open to visitors, so access is marked restricted. The 2021 article's staffing outcome is not confirmed beyond the June 9 statement. Search snippets mention a Whitman Ranger District phone number, a Wikipedia elevation of 8,325 ft and a 2021 Blue Mountain Eagle version; none were read, so none are used. Reads: 6 pages (NHLR, firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts, 2023 visit page, 2021 La Grande Observer article); 2 web searches.
